claims.text: CALPHAD-assisted high-throughput DTA coupled with in situ XRD can determine melting temperature across diverse high-entropy-alloy systems.
The proposed method can determine enthalpy of fusion across diverse high-entropy-alloy systems.
The proposed method can determine entropy of fusion across diverse high-entropy-alloy systems.
The proposed method can determine volume change at melting across diverse high-entropy-alloy systems.
Melting-related quantities can be measured with uncertainties below ±2%.
Structural transitions observed by XRD will correlate directly with latent-heat changes measured by DTA.
A solid-state library of CoCrFeMnNi derivatives can be prepared with uniform microstructures for high-throughput testing.
DTA can be conducted under argon at controlled heating and cooling rates to measure phase transformations.
Calibration against known melting temperatures and transformation enthalpies can refine DTA temperature and sensitivity measurements.
Heating rates of 5–50 K/min are suitable for capturing rapid phase transitions in the proposed HEA library.
An inert atmosphere prevents oxidation or contamination during the measurements.
Disappearance, shifting, or broadening of diffraction peaks identifies the crystalline-to-liquid transition.
DTA endothermic and exothermic peaks can identify transformations and quantify their heat effects.
XRD patterns can track crystallographic transformations and provide unit-cell parameters from which transformation volume changes are calculated.
Integrating DTA and XRD data with CALPHAD permits accurate calculation of melting temperature, latent heat, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting volume change.
The integrated approach will yield a robust map of comprehensive liquid-phase thermodynamic properties over various HEA compositions.
The approach is primarily applicable to HEAs with sharp, well-defined melting transitions and may be less applicable to systems with sluggish kinetics or broad transitions.

The approach is falsified if measured melting temperature, latent heat, or volume change differs from known baselines by more than ±2%, or if XRD and DTA transition indicators disagree by more than 10%.
